A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CARE dataset and cultural preference-learning study. Their main text, tables, figures, equations and complete appendices are readable, including the annotation screenshots, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original human preference annotations, model-alignment experiments, cultural and general NLP evaluations, and analyses of language choice and geographic scope.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, expanded Japanese-model experiments, overlap and response-length analyses, and repeated-inference results.

M1.justification: Both versions construct preference pairs from the highest- and lowest-rated responses and apply the same DPO, KTO and SimPO procedures. v5's displayed objectives explain existing algorithms; its additional Swallow models extend experimental configurations without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: v5 adds natively collected Chinese and Japanese general-purpose preference training data from HelpSteer3, supplementing the translated synthetic preference controls. CARE's cultures and categories, BLEND, INCLUDE and the general NLP evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 4 newly evaluates DPO with HelpSteer3, which v3 only discussed as related work. v5 Table 16 also adds UltraFeedback- and HelpSteer3-aligned comparators to the existing BLEND evaluation, where v3 Figure 4 compared vanilla and CARE-aligned models. The original comparator groups remain.

E3.justification: v5 adds Gemma/Mistral Swallow configurations and HelpSteer3 training experiments using 1.1k Chinese and 0.2k Japanese pairs. Its new overlap audit uses embedding-based nearest-neighbor selection followed by manual checking. The existing CARE splits, training hyperparameters and judging prompts are retained.

E4.justification: v5 substantially broadens diagnostic coverage through a train-test paraphrase-overlap audit (A.4), response-length analysis (A.5/Figure 7), and repeated-inference robustness check (C.3). It also expands the existing Japanese pretraining-plus-alignment analysis from Llama Swallow to Gemma and Mistral families. Earlier geographic-scope and general-capability checks remain.

E5.justification: Beyond v3's annotation-agreement and judge-correlation reporting, v5 C.3/Table 15 reports three inference runs per prompt for vanilla and CARE-aligned Gemma2-9B across all three languages, with mean ± standard deviation. This is a limited uncertainty assessment; repeated training runs, seeds and significance tests are not reported.

E6.justification: Substantial additions include HelpSteer3 scores, Gemma/Mistral Swallow results, Swallow-8B's +2.0-point Japanese INCLUDE result, BLEND comparator scores, and diagnostic outcomes including 6/4/3 Chinese/Arabic/Japanese paraphrase overlaps. Swallow-70B's average changes from 6.76 in v3 Table 12 to 7.30 in v5 Table 5, but its changed backbone description prevents treating this as an established same-setting gain. Most original matched results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v5 Section 4.1 writes out objectives for the same established DPO, KTO and SimPO algorithms already used in v3. This expands mathematical explanation without adding substantive theoretical results, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The main CARE contribution and claims about data efficiency, initial model strength and cross-cultural alignment remain. The introduction and Section 4.2 narrow the generic-preference comparison from outperforming to competitive or stronger performance and complementary benefits, although the abstract retains the stronger wording.

C2.justification: v5 interprets the expanded Swallow results as supporting cultural alignment even after strong language specialization, characterizes residual paraphrase overlap as minimal and realistic, and interprets repeated inference as supporting robustness. The limitations also qualify universally shared topics as generally shared and refine the consensus/neutrality framing.

D1.justification: The abstract changes CARE's reported availability from a planned release to publicly available. Appendix B adds explicit dataset-to-repository mappings and native versus translated/synthetic provenance. v5 also documents duplicate handling and overlap-check implementation, and clarifies snippet-containing paragraph extraction for the existing search experiment. Core training and inference details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds focused references on cultural alignment, safety, consensus and values, including Rystrøm et al., Qiu et al., Bakker et al. and Huang et al. It removes the Ma and Okazaki Swallow references and replaces the Qwen2 report citation with Qwen2.5. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v5 shortens the title, adds a Sony AI affiliation and acknowledgments, and locally rewrites the introduction, related work and limitations. Section 4.1 gains objective explanations; the language-specific analysis moves from Appendix D.1 to Section 4.6, alongside new appendix subsections. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v3's small appendix Swallow table becomes an expanded main-text table grouped by model family. v5 adds Figure 7 and Tables 12, 15 and 16 for response lengths, provenance, repeated runs and BLEND comparisons. Table 4 gains a HelpSteer3 row; Figure 4 gains Swallow bars and a revised Arabic axis. Most displays and the two-column layout remain.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3, the native-human baseline, broader Japanese controls, overlap audit and repeated-inference results make the empirical conclusions easier to assess; provenance and reported dataset availability also improve reproducibility. The gain is limited: repetition covers only Gemma2-9B, and Section 4.6 newly claims 0.2–0.4-point benefits although Table 5 shows a 0.10-point gain for Gemma-Swallow.
